gaps.sentence: ___ noise woke me up in the middle of the night.
gaps.explanation: 'The noise' — the one that woke me; 'in the night' is a fixed phrase.

gaps.sentence: ___ water in this bottle tastes strange.
gaps.explanation: The of/in-phrase makes the noun definite: the water in this bottle.

gaps.sentence: He received ___ OBE in the New Year's Honours list.
gaps.explanation: 'OBE' is pronounced /əʊ biː iː/, starting with a vowel sound, so 'an' is used.
'The capital of Italy' — the of-phrase makes it unique and definite.

gaps.sentence: She was appointed ___ managing director at just thirty-four.
gaps.explanation: After 'appoint/elect/name + unique role' no article is used.

gaps.sentence: They sailed across ___ Mediterranean last summer.
gaps.explanation: Seas and oceans take 'the': the Mediterranean.

gaps.sentence: He was ___ last person to leave the building.
gaps.explanation: Ordinals take 'the': the last person, the first time.

gaps.sentence: She has ___ excellent command of Japanese.
gaps.explanation: 'Have an excellent command of' — 'excellent' starts with a vowel sound.
